why: Past the slice the deadlines' ask is stepped GRASS_STEP at a time and the loop stops at the first step past it; stepped whole it stops on it. The ask is met either way - the stepped way places up to 249 candidates more (0.1 ms here) - and no clock is read in that pace, so the step size only matters where the time is (a cell due now). One step size for both paces, kept.

name: FB1021B-a-cell-whose-slot-went-is-held-done
why: Reached only on a field with fewer slots than its disc (AUDIT PERF10 F1's test seam; the game's bound is the swept one), when the cell a slot was asked for at its begin is no longer nearer than any standing one at its end. Dropped, it is begun again from the world as it stands; held, it is written when a slot frees or dropped when it leaves reach - the same cell, the same bytes, and the field at rest the same (48 starved walks, 10 such cells, none left either way). Begun again is kept: the world it was placed from may have moved.

name: AUDIT-FB1021B-F1-the-pace-is-timed-without-a-cell-due-now
why: The pace's time is kept only to be taken off the frame's time, and the frame's time is read only on a frame with a cell due now (`now && clock() - t0 - paced < budgetMs`; `now` is fixed before the loop). Timed without one, a step reads the clock twice more and `paced` is never read: the same candidates, the same cells. Kept so a ride with no cell due now reads no clock in its pace, as FB1021B's did.
